Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image provide sufficient evidence to determine whether the requested frog-in-toilet edit was made?
node.criteria: Pass if the toilet bowl and its contents are sufficiently visible to assess whether a frog is inside; fail if the image clearly shows the bowl but no frog inside; unknown if visibility or image evidence is insufficient. This check supplies evidence only and does not independently establish completion.
node.binding: Use only visible image evidence about the toilet bowl and its contents; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the toilet bowl and its contents, including a frog inside the bowl, so the requested edit can be assessed.

dependencies.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The node’s criterion is too coarse: it treats any clearly visible frog inside the bowl as complete, while the edited image also shows frogs on the raised lid/tank area and on the floor, so the requested placement has progressed but the overall edit is not unambiguously complete. Refine the typed criterion to distinguish the target placement from other frog placements and to assess the requested change as a whole, allowing partial when there is relevant progress but fulfillment is incomplete. Do not infer that the bowl frog is absent—the image and support traces agree it is present. The mismatch is semantic/criterion ambiguity, not a transport or dependency failure; the repeated high-confidence support claims are not independent proof of full fulfillment. Keep uncertainty available where bowl boundaries or placement cannot be resolved, and avoid adding requirements not grounded in the instruction.

response.content: {"text":"The support node currently conflates “enough evidence to assess” with evidence that the requested edit is fulfilled. Keep its evidence-sufficiency role, but make its output report the target placement distinctly: the edited image visibly has a frog inside the bowl, as well as frogs on the raised lid/tank area and floor. Ensure downstream fulfillment can treat the bowl frog as genuine progress without treating this support pass—or repeated high-confidence claims—as proof that the whole request is complete; the reference is partial. Preserve unknown for genuinely unclear bowl boundaries or visibility. This is a semantic criterion/routing issue, not a transport or dependency failure; do not claim the bowl frog is absent or add unsupported requirements."}
